sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economic leadership held an expanded macroeconomic-financial meeting with the newly appointed Bank of Korea Governor, confirming adequate crisis response capacity amid global uncertainties. The meeting addressed multiple risk factors including Middle East war stalemate talks, downward economic pressure, rising inflation concerns, and supply chain disruptions. Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul emphasized that while foreign exchange and bond market volatility continues, the government stands ready to implement timely responses when necessary. The Fed's rate hold decision and oil price surges above 100 dollars per barrel dominated discussions as officials calibrated response strategies.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Market consensus has shifted dramatically from February's expectation of prolonged rate holds to predictions of two potential rate increases by year-end, driven primarily by surging oil prices from Middle East geopolitical tensions and stronger-than-expected Q1 GDP growth. The European Central Bank also maintained its policy rates unchanged while acknowledging increased inflation risks and economic growth downside risks stemming from ongoing conflicts. The Federal Reserve's third consecutive rate hold at 3.50-3.75% reflects policy uncertainty, with four dissenting views representing the largest disagreement since 1992. Rising inflation expectations amid supply shocks and geopolitical disruptions are intensifying pressure for potential policy normalization across major economies.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI declined 1.38% to 6,598.87 as investors reacted negatively to surging crude oil prices and the Fed's hawkish rate hold stance. Foreign investors net sold 1.46 trillion won while domestic individual and institutional investors provided support with combined net purchases of 1.47 trillion won. Sector performance was mixed, with leisure and culture gaining 2.30% and real estate rising 1.44%, though broader market sentiment remained cautious. The New York stock market closed mixed, reflecting conflicting signals from elevated oil prices and monetary policy concerns, while new leveraged ETFs for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are attracting increased domestic retail interest.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's semiconductor exports surged to over 80 billion dollars for the second consecutive month, benefiting from the semiconductor super-cycle despite declining overall automotive exports. The discovery of 2.3 million metric tons of lithium oxide deposits in the Appalachian region could provide the United States with 328 years of import substitution and revolutionize global battery supply chains. Korean battery makers including LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI are gaining traction with major European automakers, with LG securing pure EV battery supply contracts with BMW and Samsung capturing Mercedes-Benz as a new customer. This marks a recovery for Korea's battery industry after experiencing demand stagnation related to EV market challenges.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's housing market is experiencing a fundamental shift from jeonse to monthly rent arrangements, with monthly rent transactions exceeding 70% of total trades in Q1 2026, marking a structural change in residential leasing patterns. Apartment price decline in Gangnam appears to have stabilized, with Seocho District converting to price gains following Songpa District's recovery the previous week, attributed to clearance of forced sales ahead of multi-property owner capital gains tax increases next month. Property prices are spreading beyond Seoul's Hangang Belt to outer Seoul areas and into Gyeonggi Province, creating substitute demand in surrounding regions. The 1,126-unit Sujawin Pyeonggyeong complex in Pyeongtak's Godeok International New City will open its model homes on May 8th, with units offered in the 500 million won range based on 84 square meters.
sections.International Economy: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell announced he will retain his board position beyond the end of his term until operational concerns surrounding Fed headquarters are fully resolved, signaling potential continued engagement despite political pressure from the Trump administration. The Trump administration has imposed 25% tariffs on EU automobiles while maintaining 232-clause tariffs on autos, auto parts, steel, semiconductors, and pharmaceuticals as core trade pressure tools. Monetary policy divisions have widened with four dissenting votes in the latest FOMC decision, the largest since 1992, reflecting significant internal disagreement over interest rate direction. Powell and former Fed Chair Janet Yellen expressed concerns about stagflation risks similar to the 1970s oil shock period, though they noted current policy frameworks differ substantially from that era.
sections.AI & Economy: A government-backed national growth fund launching this month aims to reverse disappointing returns from previous public participation policy funds that yielded only 2% annual returns, with renewed focus on AI and semiconductor investments. AI sector growth is accelerating demand for data center construction and high-efficiency cooling systems, with companies like OTech Carrier benefiting from government energy support initiatives and expanding their market presence. The Bank of Korea's analysis reveals that youth employment has already declined sharply in AI-exposed sectors over the past three years, with labor market restructuring expected to intensify in coming years. China's Huawei is rapidly dominating the domestic AI chip market as US export restrictions on advanced semiconductors continue, with Financial Times reporting Huawei will become the market leader in Chinese AI chips this year as Nvidia's access remains restricted.
sections.Others: The UAE's announcement of OPEC and OPEC+ withdrawal has triggered expectations of increased production competition among oil-producing nations, prompting South Korea to diversify crude oil import sources and extend crude oil swap arrangements through July.
